title: The Orbit of the Kuiper Line
premise: Orsen Thornbury is a memory-clone of a murdered colonial magistrate, activated eleven years after the original's death to inherit an unsolved case on Kuiper Line, a failing mining colony the two rival fleets have quietly written off. When a woman named Sera Voss appears on the manifest of a ship that never flew, Orsen discovers the original's murder was staged to hide a massacre that both fleets' peace treaty depends on denying. As the colony's life support fails and Sera — who turns out to be the original Thornbury's daughter, living under a false name — forces the truth into the open, Orsen must choose between preserving the lie that keeps two fleets from war and honoring the justice his template died for. In the end, Orsen broadcasts the truth alongside evidence framing no one but the dead, letting both fleets blame a ghost, and chooses to stay behind on Kuiper Line as its last witness rather than escape as a copy of someone else.
about_author: Ansel Pemberton is the pen name of a former maritime records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing ships that were decommissioned before they ever sailed. They write science fiction about paperwork, ghosts, and the people history forgets to kill properly.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Orsen Thornbury wakes in a cloning vat on Kuiper Line with his template's memories ending mid-murder. The colony administrator, Dree Halvard, hands him the dead man's case files and a warning: nobody wants this solved. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: disorientation and the loneliness of inheriting a stranger's grief.

chapters.title: The Colony That Forgot Its Own Name
chapters.summary: Orsen tours Kuiper Line's dying infrastructure — cracked domes, rationed air, children born who've never seen open sky. He interviews witnesses who remember his face and flinch. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: mounting dread as he realizes the colony itself is a crime scene slowly being erased.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing port manifests, Orsen finds the freighter Calyx Meridian listed as departed with full crew — yet it was scrapped in dock. One name on the manifest doesn't match any crew record: Sera Voss. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the first crack of intrigue; a puzzle piece that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Manifest
chapters.summary: Sera Voss arrives on the colony shuttle, unannounced, asking for the late Magistrate Thornbury by name. She studies Orsen's cloned face without fear or surprise. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: guarded recognition — she knows exactly what he is, and she came anyway.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Kept
chapters.summary: Sera reveals she found her father's hidden data cache years ago but couldn't decrypt it alone. It references 'the Calyx count' — a passenger list that contradicts official casualty figures for a fleet incident called the Verity Break. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: reluctant trust between two people using each other.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Orsen learns the political stakes: the Armistice Fleet and the Concord hold their ceasefire together because each believes the other committed the Verity Break massacre — and neither can investigate without war. The original Thornbury was killed for getting too close. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: vertigo at the scale of what one small case sits beneath.

chapters.title: Ration Days
chapters.summary: Life support failures accelerate; Halvard begs Orsen to drop the case so evacuation negotiations with the Concord can proceed. A riot over water rations kills three colonists. POV: Halvard. Emotional beat: her exhausted pragmatism versus guilt — she knows more than she says.

chapters.title: The Cache Opens
chapters.summary: Sera and Orsen decrypt the cache: the original's field recordings prove the Calyx Meridian carried refugees secretly evacuated during the Verity Break, then was destroyed with all aboard to bury the evidence. Both fleets share the guilt. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: horror curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Someone Else Is Reading
chapters.summary: Their quarters are searched; the cache copy is nearly stolen by a Concord intelligence agent embedded as a dock worker. Orsen realizes both fleets have kept watchers on Kuiper Line for eleven years. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening; nowhere is neutral ground.

chapters.title: Halvard's Confession
chapters.summary: Halvard admits she helped falsify the death report of the original Thornbury under orders, believing silence would buy the colony evacuation priority. The evacuation never came. POV: Halvard. Emotional beat: shame and self-deception laid bare; loyalty as a slow poison.

chapters.title: The Clone Question
chapters.summary: Sera confronts Orsen: is he pursuing justice for the colony, or performing his template's life? Their argument turns intimate — she confesses he is not her father, and she is glad of it. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: raw honesty; identity examined and, for once, accepted.

chapters.title: Concord Summons
chapters.summary: A Concord cruiser arrives offering full evacuation for every colonist — if Orsen surrenders the cache and declares the case closed. Halvard urges acceptance. The colonists vote, torn between survival and truth. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: temptation made institutional; justice priced in lives.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: In a freezing assembly hall, the colony votes narrowly to refuse the deal and demand investigation instead. Orsen publicly commits to broadcasting the Calyx evidence within thirty days. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: fragile collective courage; a community choosing dignity over rescue.

chapters.title: Armistice Shadow
chapters.summary: The Armistice Fleet responds by blockading the colony, claiming Concord coercion. An Armistice officer, Captain Iye Okafor, privately tells Orsen her fleet wants the truth too — if it can be shaped to blame only Concord. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: seduction of a usable lie.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: The colony's oxygen recyclers fail in a pattern too precise for accident. Sera traces the sabotage code to Concord intelligence — they intend the colony's death to close the case permanently. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: cold fury; grief for a home she barely knew.

chapters.title: Thirteen Hours of Air
chapters.summary: With life support collapsing, Orsen negotiates a temporary repair truce between Okafor's engineers and Concord agents, trading himself as hostage guarantee. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into purpose; a clone becoming his own kind of magistrate.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Decision
chapters.summary: Okafor offers Orsen a doctored version of the evidence implicating only Concord — war would follow, but the colony would be avenged and evacuated. Sera argues for the whole truth even if it frees the guilty. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: the book's moral crux, argued with love and anger.

chapters.title: What the Original Would Do
chapters.summary: Orsen plays the template's final recording: the dead magistrate anticipated his own murder and left instructions — publish everything, protect no faction, accept the cost. Orsen realizes he has been waiting for permission to differ. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: inheritance completed by refusal; identity claimed, not received.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: From the colony's ancient relay array, Orsen transmits the complete Calyx record to both fleets and the civilian nets simultaneously. Both fleets scramble; blockade guns power up; Halvard opens the dome shields so nothing can be recalled. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: terrible calm at the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Ghost Verdict
chapters.summary: Facing mutual exposure, both fleets seize the exit Orsen built into the broadcast: evidence framing the long-dead original conspirators for the massacre and the cover-up. War stands down; investigations target the dead. Justice outside the law, imperfect and real. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: bitter relief; truth surviving as compromise.

chapters.title: Evacuation of the Living
chapters.summary: Ships from both fleets evacuate Kuiper Line together, an unplanned joint operation. Halvard stays to sign the colony's formal closure as its last administrator; Sera asks Orsen to come with her to the inner worlds. POV: Halvard. Emotional beat: farewell without erasure; a community dispersed but remembered.

chapters.title: The Orbit of the Kuiper Line
chapters.summary: Orsen declines passage, remaining aboard the derelict relay station to maintain the archive of the Calyx dead and the colony's records — the first witness in history to choose his own orbit. Sera promises to return. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; a copy who became an original by staying.
